People think that getting circular breathing down is among the hardest things one can learn to do - but it's really easy to learn! People think that it's inhaling while exhaling, which is kind of true, but that kind of paints a weird picture.

What's really going on is inflating your cheeks and using your cheek muscles to blow out air and using that air as a sort of 'reserve' while inhaling through your nose. It should be noted your cheek muscles have to build up to this, and it's kind of based on muscle memory. The easiest way to learn how is when you're taking a shower, you fill your mouth with water, then use your cheeks to push out a thin and steady stream of water through your lips. While doing this, breathe in through your nose. This will build your cheek muscles up. Try to push it all out as quickly as you can, but fill your lungs with air while breathing in through your nose in the same amount of time. After doing this for a bit, it will soon become muscle memory.
